lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Transformer un discours direct en discours indirect.
Appliquer la concordance des temps et le changement des repères.
reviewNotes: Niveau et sélection des points de langue à confronter au programme officiel d'anglais de Tle A.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Les changements de temps
blocks.md:
Quand le verbe introducteur est au **passé** (*said, told, asked*), le temps recule d'un cran :
- present simple → **past simple**
- present continuous → **past continuous**
- past simple → **past perfect**
- present perfect → **past perfect**
- will → **would** ; can → **could** ; may → **might**
Exemple : *« I am tired »* → She said **she was** tired.

blocks.title: Les changements de repères
blocks.md:
Pronoms : *I → he/she*, *my → his/her*. Repères : *today → that day*, *tomorrow → the next day*, *yesterday → the day before*, *now → then*, *here → there*, *this → that*, *ago → before*.

On n'écrit plus de guillemets ni de point d'interrogation dans une question indirecte.

blocks.title: Questions, ordres, demandes
blocks.md:
- **Question fermée** : *if / whether* : « Do you like tea? » → He asked **if** I liked tea.
- **Question ouverte** : mot interrogatif + ordre normal : « Where do you live? » → She asked **where I lived**.
- **Ordre** : *told + objet + to* : « Sit down! » → He **told me to sit** down.
- **Demande** : *asked + objet + to*.

blocks.caption: Quelques équivalences à connaître.
blocks.alt: Un tableau : am ou is devient was, will devient would, tomorrow devient the next day, now devient then.

blocks.title: Erreurs fréquentes
blocks.md:
- Garder l'**ordre interrogatif** : ✗ She asked where did I live ; ✓ *where I lived*.
- Oublier de changer **pronoms et repères**.
- Écrire *said me* : on dit **told me** ou **said to me**.
- Mettre *that* après *told* sans objet : *told that* est faux.
- Reculer le temps quand le verbe introducteur est **au présent** (*He says he is tired*) : inutile.

blocks.title: Exemple 1 : affirmation
blocks.statement: Rapportez : Ngu said, « I will visit my aunt tomorrow. »
steps: Verbe introducteur au passé : will → would ; my → his ; tomorrow → the next day.
Ngu said that he would visit his aunt the next day.
blocks.answer: Ngu said that he would visit his aunt the next day.

blocks.title: Exemple 2 : question
blocks.statement: Rapportez : Her teacher asked, « Where did you put the books? »
steps: Question ouverte : ordre normal sujet-verbe, past simple → past perfect.
Her teacher asked where she had put the books.
blocks.answer: Her teacher asked where she had put the books.

objectives: Choisir who, which, whose, that, where, when.
reviewNotes: Niveau et sélection des points de langue à confronter au programme officiel d'anglais de Tle A.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Les pronoms relatifs
blocks.md:
- **who** : personnes (sujet) : *the man who lives next door*.
- **whom** : personnes (objet, plus formel).
- **which** : choses et animaux.
- **that** : personnes ou choses (relative déterminative).
- **whose** : possession : *the girl whose bag was stolen*.
- **where** (lieu), **when** (temps), **why** (raison).

blocks.title: Déterminative et explicative
blocks.md:
La relative **déterminative** précise de qui ou de quoi on parle ; **pas de virgule**, *that* possible : *The book that I bought is old.*

La relative **explicative** ajoute une information ; **entre virgules**, *that* impossible : *My brother, who lives in Douala, is a nurse.*

blocks.caption: Le relatif dépend de l'antécédent.
blocks.alt: Un tableau : personne who ou that, chose which ou that, possession whose, lieu where.

blocks.title: Supprimer le relatif
blocks.md: Quand le relatif est **objet** d'une relative déterminative, on peut le supprimer : *The film (that) we saw was great.* On **ne peut pas** le supprimer s'il est **sujet** : *The man who called you is here.*

blocks.title: Erreurs fréquentes
blocks.md:
- Dire **which** pour une personne.
- Mettre une **virgule** devant une relative déterminative.
- Employer **that** après une virgule.
- Oublier **whose** et dire *who's* (qui est).
- Ajouter un **pronom en trop** : ✗ the book which I bought it.

blocks.title: Exemple 1 : choisir
blocks.statement: Complétez : The teacher ___ taught us last year has moved to Bamenda.
steps: L'antécédent est une personne et le relatif est sujet : who (ou that).

blocks.title: Exemple 2 : relier
blocks.statement: Reliez : This is the village. My grandmother was born there.
steps: This is the village where my grandmother was born.
blocks.answer: This is the village where my grandmother was born.
